How dependencies flow

Layers come from the package dependency graph: a package only imports packages in rows below its own. ▲ nothing imports it (an entry point), ▼ it imports nothing else here (a leaf). Groups with no import path between them — the frontend, for instance — are independent and simply occupy their own rows; the right-hand label is the row's dominant domain. Click a package to open it in the graph.

Repository Areas

Measured findings, worst first. Everything here is derived from the same scan as the rest of the map — no hand-maintained lists.

Layered dependency graph (Sugiyama: cycle condensation → Coffman–Graham layering → dummy-node routing → median/transpose crossing reduction). A node sits below everything that imports it, so depth reads top → bottom and arrows point importer → dependency. Click a node to isolate its edges.

UML generalization (class inheritance) for base classes that resolve inside this repository; external bases such as Protocol or Exception are left out. Read it the UML way: the hollow triangle points at the base class, and a subclass always sits below the class it extends. Click a class to open its module.

Pick a module or open one from the Tree / a drawer.

Center = selected module. Left/outgoing = modules it imports, right/incoming = modules that import it (arrows point importer → dependency). Click a node to re-center; drag to rearrange; wheel to zoom. Dimmed nodes sit outside the selected package.
